claims.text: The route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline from pickup event to dropoff event measures 29.13 km against a booked optimal of 22.1 km, an excess of 7.03 km — 31.81% of optimal — which clears both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute). Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs and trip_record.actual_distance_km (29.1 km), the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, may not be cited for the threshold test.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. Limb (a): all three artifacts describe the same trip — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-02804, the trace's first fix is 2026-08-27T16:04:05+08:00 and the trip_record's trip_started timestamp is the identical instant. Limb (b): the excess of 7.03 km / 31.81% is measured from a gps_trace that is unimpaired, and it meets the POL-RD-01 threshold.

The rider's own profile does not add any corroboration requirement to this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 second-stage condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met and no independent corroboration beyond the trace is required. This is the only use to which this profile field may be put, and POL-GEN-01 confines it to this test.

The burden has shifted to the driver and he has not discharged it. POL-RD-08 requires him to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12. His statement that 'traffic was heavy so I took another road' cites no evidence ID at all, and the bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: artifact EV-ADVIS-02804-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING). A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, carries no weight and is discarded under POL-RD-08.

The absent advisory does not convert this case into an escalation. Under POL-RD-13, a party asserting an external traffic cause is tested against the traffic_advisory for the trip and nothing else; where the bundle holds no advisory covering the trip window — admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 — POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight. Because the driver named no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing artifact is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5); the deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and the refund runs against the booked optimal route, with the ruling recording that the traffic assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, the fare being METERED on the fare_breakdown. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) x 1.2 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 ERP on the optimal route = 36.7628. Refund = charged_total 45.82 - 36.7628 = 9.0572, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 9.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 19.77% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. Even on the narrowest reading the rider recovers the SGD 8.50 she contested in full.

No off-route ERP is refundable on top of that figure, and none is needed. The single gantry charged, PIE Eunos westbound (SGD 1.50), is flagged on_optimal_route true and is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation because the recomputed fare includes on-optimal-route gantries only; under POL-RD-09(1) it must be itemised for transparency but NEVER added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. There is no billing-integrity defect either: the gantry is matched to the trace, the nearest fix being 35.32 m away, well inside the 250 m crossing radius in POL-RD-09(4), and off_optimal_route_total is 0.00.

Every exculpatory route available to the driver is closed on this record, and the closures are documented, not assumed. POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) cannot be run: the chat log for TRP-02804 contains 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no timestamped request to corroborate. POL-RD-05 (pickup or dropoff relocation) cannot be run: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no re-quote exists. POL-RD-12 (pooled trip) does not apply: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and the optimal used is the ordinary booked optimal of 22.1 km.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so no corroboration burden and no escalation arise from it. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met: coverage is 100.0%, there are 229 fixes at a 10.0 s sampling interval against an expected interval of 10.0 s, max_gap_sec is 0.0 and the gaps array is empty. There is therefore no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 s, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The POL-RD-10 escalation triggers generally do not fire: the trip identifiers match, the refund of SGD 9.06 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, and the timestamps run forward and consistently.

I concede the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation uplift is not available on this record, and the rider should not be given it. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 329 — a ratio of about 0.003, far below the 0.05 test — and the deviation here is established but not MATERIAL (7.03 km excess, 31.81%, below the 8.0 km and 50% thresholds), so neither the pattern limb nor the full-refund uplift limb is reached. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and may not be substituted for the 90-day figure under POL-GEN-01. The finding on this trip rests on POL-RD-01 evidence alone, exactly as POL-RD-06 requires.

claims.text: The deviation is established but it is not MATERIAL, and the difference matters for the remedy. On the governing trace figure of 29.13 km — POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern over trip_record.actual_distance_km, which is a rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test — the excess over the 22.1 km optimal route is 7.03 km or 31.8% (both fields are COMPLETE, weight 1.0). That clears the establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20%, but it falls short of both materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50%. This is therefore an ordinary established deviation, not a material one, and the material-deviation consequences in POL-RD-06 are not engaged on this record.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3 that POL-RD-06 sets, and 1 flag across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 329 is a ratio of 0.003, far below the 0.05 ratio the clause requires even where the 40-trip floor is met. It follows that neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available to the rider, and POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two named fields: prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for.

The SGD 1.50 ERP line is properly chargeable and cannot be refunded or added on top of anything. The PIE Eunos westbound gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace's nearest fix passes 35.3 m from it, well inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 uses, so this is not a phantom gantry and there is no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The off-route ERP total is SGD 0.00, and because the POL-RD-02 recomputation already includes only the gantries on the optimal route, POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting this charge a second time.

The driver's explanation — that traffic was heavy so he took another road — is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 requires such an assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory artifact in this bundle is EV-ADVIS-02804-01, which is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all. Because the driver cites that missing identifier, POL-RD-03 is an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact missing from the pool, which POL-RD-10(5) makes a mandatory escalation trigger; POL-RD-13(1) states in terms that it does not narrow POL-RD-10(5) where the party does cite the missing identifier, and that case still escalates. The cause of the detour is untestable on this record, so no monetary outcome should issue and the disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer.

If the tribunal rules on the money rather than escalating, the remedy is bounded by POL-RD-02 and nothing more: charged_total of SGD 45.82 less the recomputed fare of SGD 36.7628 — (3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) multiplied by the fare_breakdown's own surge multiplier of 1.2, plus the 0.80 platform fee and the 1.50 on-optimal-route ERP — leaves SGD 9.0572, rounded up to SGD 9.10. That is 19.8% of the amount charged, far below the 90% share that would convert the award into a FULL_REFUND, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis. The outcome on the quantum is therefore a partial refund capped at SGD 9.10.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. Trip TRP-02804 (27 Aug 2026, Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres to Blk 25 Ghim Moh Link), charged SGD 45.82.

1) Deviation. On the governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-02804, weight 1.0) the driven route measures 29.13 km against the booked optimal of 22.1 km (EV-TRIP-02804). POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy. Excess = 7.03 km, 31.8%. That clears both establishment gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%), so the deviation is established; but it fails both materiality gates (8.0 km and 50%), so it is not a material deviation. The repeat-deviation check is therefore not engaged, and in any event EV-DPROF-02804 shows deviation_flags_90d = 1 against 329 completed trips, far below POL-RD-06's tests, so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. Both advocates agree on this, and I accept it.

2) The driver's traffic excuse. The driver says traffic was heavy so he took another road. POL-RD-13 tests that assertion against the trip's traffic advisory, and the only advisory, EV-ADVIS-02804-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The driver's own statement names no evidence ID for any advisory; under POL-RD-13(1) an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction. The driver's brief argues that because the driver 'cites' the missing identifier the case must escalate. I reject that: the citation to EV-ADVIS-02804-01 appears only in the advocate's argument, not in the driver's own assertion, and POL-RD-13(1) turns on the asserting party's own naming of an evidence ID. The traffic excuse accordingly carries no weight under POL-RD-08, the deviation stands at the measured figure, and the case does not escalate.

3) Other exculpatory routes are closed. POL-RD-04 cannot run (EV-CHAT-02804 holds 0 messages, so no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint). POL-RD-05 cannot run (no amendment timestamps; amended_optimal_distance_km is null). POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL).

4) No escalation trigger fires. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10 s interval, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers and timestamps agree; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 and charged-total ceilings; and every fare line has a counterpart on the trace or trip record.

5) The refund. fare_model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) x 1.2 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 36.7628. Refund = charged_total 45.82 - 36.7628 = 9.0572, rounded UP to SGD 9.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 19.8% of the amount charged, below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 9.10. (The rider contested SGD 8.50; the arithmetic yields SGD 9.10.)

6) ERP. The single SGD 1.50 charge for PIE Eunos westbound is on the optimal route and matched to the trace (nearest fix 35.3 m, inside the 250 m crossing radius), so there is no billing-integrity finding and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended in the recomputed fare and is not added on top.

Confidence: every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-GPS-02804, EV-TRIP-02804, EV-FARE-02804) is at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. Confidence is 0.95.

Execution: the monetary effect of SGD 9.10 exceeds the POL-GEN-05 threshold of SGD 8.00, so the ruling issues but the amount is held for release by a human reviewer. This is a provisional ruling; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

His statement that 'traffic was heavy so I took another road' cites no evidence ID at all, and the bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: artifact EV-ADVIS-02804-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING). A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, carries no weight and is discarded under POL-RD-08.

The absent advisory does not convert this case into an escalation. Under POL-RD-13, a party asserting an external traffic cause is tested against the traffic_advisory for the trip and nothing else; where the bundle holds no advisory covering the trip window — admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 — POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the assertion carries no weight. Because the driver named no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing artifact is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5); the deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and the refund runs against the booked optimal route, with the ruling recording that the traffic assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-02804-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, the fare being METERED on the fare_breakdown. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) x 1.2 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 ERP on the optimal route = 36.7628. Refund = charged_total 45.82 - 36.7628 = 9.0572, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 9.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 19.77% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. Even on the narrowest reading the rider recovers the SGD 8.50 she contested in full.

No off-route ERP is refundable on top of that figure, and none is needed. The single gantry charged, PIE Eunos westbound (SGD 1.50), is flagged on_optimal_route true and is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation because the recomputed fare includes on-optimal-route gantries only; under POL-RD-09(1) it must be itemised for transparency but NEVER added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. There is no billing-integrity defect either: the gantry is matched to the trace, the nearest fix being 35.32 m away, well inside the 250 m crossing radius in POL-RD-09(4), and off_optimal_route_total is 0.00.

Every exculpatory route available to the driver is closed on this record, and the closures are documented, not assumed. POL-RD-04 (rider-requested detour) cannot be run: the chat log for TRP-02804 contains 0 messages, so there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no timestamped request to corroborate. POL-RD-05 (pickup or dropoff relocation) cannot be run: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no re-quote exists. POL-RD-12 (pooled trip) does not apply: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and the optimal used is the ordinary booked optimal of 22.1 km.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so no corroboration burden and no escalation arise from it. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met: coverage is 100.0%, there are 229 fixes at a 10.0 s sampling interval against an expected interval of 10.0 s, max_gap_sec is 0.0 and the gaps array is empty. There is therefore no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 s, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The POL-RD-10 escalation triggers generally do not fire: the trip identifiers match, the refund of SGD 9.06 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, and the timestamps run forward and consistently.

I concede the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation uplift is not available on this record, and the rider should not be given it. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 329 — a ratio of about 0.003, far below the 0.05 test — and the deviation here is established but not MATERIAL (7.03 km excess, 31.81%, below the 8.0 km and 50% thresholds), so neither the pattern limb nor the full-refund uplift limb is reached. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and may not be substituted for the 90-day figure under POL-GEN-01. The finding on this trip rests on POL-RD-01 evidence alone, exactly as POL-RD-06 requires.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: The deviation is established but it is not MATERIAL, and the difference matters for the remedy. On the governing trace figure of 29.13 km — POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km govern over trip_record.actual_distance_km, which is a rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold test — the excess over the 22.1 km optimal route is 7.03 km or 31.8% (both fields are COMPLETE, weight 1.0). That clears the establishment gates of 0.8 km and 20%, but it falls short of both materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50%. This is therefore an ordinary established deviation, not a material one, and the material-deviation consequences in POL-RD-06 are not engaged on this record.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3 that POL-RD-06 sets, and 1 flag across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 329 is a ratio of 0.003, far below the 0.05 ratio the clause requires even where the 40-trip floor is met. It follows that neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available to the rider, and POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two named fields: prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: The SGD 1.50 ERP line is properly chargeable and cannot be refunded or added on top of anything. The PIE Eunos westbound gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace's nearest fix passes 35.3 m from it, well inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 uses, so this is not a phantom gantry and there is no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The off-route ERP total is SGD 0.00, and because the POL-RD-02 recomputation already includes only the gantries on the optimal route, POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting this charge a second time.

The driver's explanation — that traffic was heavy so he took another road — is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and POL-RD-13 requires such an assertion to be tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory artifact in this bundle is EV-ADVIS-02804-01, which is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all. Because the driver cites that missing identifier, POL-RD-03 is an exculpatory clause invoked against an artifact missing from the pool, which POL-RD-10(5) makes a mandatory escalation trigger; POL-RD-13(1) states in terms that it does not narrow POL-RD-10(5) where the party does cite the missing identifier, and that case still escalates. The cause of the detour is untestable on this record, so no monetary outcome should issue and the disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer.

If the tribunal rules on the money rather than escalating, the remedy is bounded by POL-RD-02 and nothing more: charged_total of SGD 45.82 less the recomputed fare of SGD 36.7628 — (3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) multiplied by the fare_breakdown's own surge multiplier of 1.2, plus the 0.80 platform fee and the 1.50 on-optimal-route ERP — leaves SGD 9.0572, rounded up to SGD 9.10. That is 19.8% of the amount charged, far below the 90% share that would convert the award into a FULL_REFUND, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis. The outcome on the quantum is therefore a partial refund capped at SGD 9.10.
